precepts.why:
“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Jephthah knew the record: “Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon”. He broke down the whole history to the king of Ammon, so nobody could talk him out of it. The king could have pulled that on somebody ignorant and been given the land; Jephthah said no, that is not what happened, the book of Numbers does not say that.

This is why we must know our history. People try to confuse us about the Bible in the street the same way, so prepare yourself to the search of the fathers; we are supposed to know these things so nobody can pull the wool over our eyes.

precepts.why: “Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.” Jephthah remembered the days of old: Israel coming up from Egypt, walking through the wilderness unto the Red sea and to Kadesh, sending messengers to the king of Edom and to the king of Moab, compassing their lands, pitching on the other side of Arnon, and never coming within the border of Moab. That is the knowledge handed down from the fathers and the elders, and it is what let him answer the king of Ammon. We must know our history the same way, so nobody can pull the wool over our eyes.

precepts.why: “Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.” Paul wrote it to Timothy, a young leader, because the study never stops. precepts.text: Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border, just as Jephthah rehearsed it.
precepts.point: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why: Jephthah said Israel “sent messengers unto the king of Edom, saying, Let me, I pray thee, pass through thy land: but the king of Edom would not hearken thereto.” The record in Numbers says the same: “Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border: wherefore Israel turned away from him.” Just as Jephthah rehearsed it: Israel asked passage, Edom refused, and Israel turned away and compassed the land of Edom rather than force a way through. Israel took nobody’s land on that journey until Sihon came out against them.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
The promise behind this whole history. “Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.” We know that Angel is Christ: “for my name is in him.” “But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries. For mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: and I will cut them off.”

That is what happened with Sihon. Israel asked passage; Sihon gathered all his people, pitched in Jahaz and fought against Israel; and “the Lord God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel”. The Angel went before Israel and brought them in unto the Amorites, and the Lord cut them off, as he promised. Israel did nothing to Sihon; the Lord was an enemy to Israel’s enemies.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why: Jephthah said “Sihon trusted not Israel to pass through his coast”. Moses tells why: “But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him: for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as appeareth this day.” Go verse upon precept and you see the Most High in the midst of the battle. Sihon coming out to Jahaz was not his own idea; the Lord hardened his spirit so that Israel would possess the land of the Amorites. They came against Israel, Israel did nothing to them, and the Lord delivered them into Israel’s hand.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
“so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.” Here is how: “And the Lord our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people. And we took all his cities at that time”. “From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the Lord our God delivered all unto us”.

There was not one city too strong, because the Lord and his angels were in the midst of Israel. That is how Israel got the land from Arnon even unto Jabbok: not by taking it from Moab or Ammon, but the Lord gave it in battle when Sihon came out against his people.

precepts.text: Only unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not; Israel never touched Ammon's land, which proves the king's claim false.
precepts.point: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why: “Only unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not, nor unto any place of the river Jabbok, nor unto the cities in the mountains, nor unto whatsoever the Lord our God forbad us.” Israel never touched Ammon’s land, which proves the king’s claim false. Jephthah said “Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon”, and the record agrees: Israel possessed the coasts of the Amorites “from Arnon even unto Jabbok”, and stopped where the Lord forbad. The king of Ammon was claiming what was never his; Jephthah knew the book does not say that, and nobody could talk him out of it.

precepts.text: Declaring the end from the beginning: my counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure; whoever the Most High wants to win a war is going to win it.
precepts.point: The Most High strengthens nations and weakens nations, and moves peoples in and out of lands to fulfil his word. In this last battle Israel cannot lose so long as we keep the commandments, have faith in Christ, and endure to the end; but if we stay in sin, we die with the heathen.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
“the Lord the Judge be judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.” The Lord is in the midst of every battle; nothing goes down without the Most High letting it go down. “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. Whoever the Most High wants to win a war is going to win it. World War One, the Lord was in the midst; World War Two, the Lord was in the midst; whoever he has destined to win is going to win.

That is how the Lord dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and why the king of Ammon “hearkened not unto the words of Jephthah”: the Lord had hardened their hearts not to listen, the same as he did with Sihon. The Most High strengthens nations and weakens nations, and moves peoples in and out of lands to fulfil his word. His counsel shall stand.

precepts.text: Paul could say, I have fought a good fight, because he knew a crown of righteousness was laid up for him; that is the fight Israel is in now.
precepts.point: The Most High strengthens nations and weakens nations, and moves peoples in and out of lands to fulfil his word. In this last battle Israel cannot lose so long as we keep the commandments, have faith in Christ, and endure to the end; but if we stay in sin, we die with the heathen.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
Jephthah said “whomsoever the Lord our God shall drive out from before us, them will we possess”: we will possess whatever the Most High gives us, and we are not backing down from anybody. That is the fight Israel is in now. Paul could say, “I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith”, because he knew “there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day”. The same righteous Judge Jephthah called on to judge between Israel and Ammon gives that crown, “not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.”

In this last battle Israel cannot lose so long as we keep the commandments, have faith in Christ, and endure to the end. But if we stay in sin, we die with the heathen.

precepts.text: Rachel said to Jacob, Give me children, or else I die; that is how heavy childlessness sat upon our foremothers, and that is why Jephthah's daughter bewailed her virginity.
precepts.point: And it was a custom in Israel, that the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
Why would Jephthah’s daughter bewail her virginity if she were about to die? Because the sorrow was that she could never marry or bear children. See how heavy childlessness sat upon our foremothers: “when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.” And Jacob answered, “Am I in God’s stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?”

In those days our women wanted to bring children into the world and continue the lineage; to be without children was counted a shame and a dishonour among the daughters of Israel. Rachel would rather die than be without children. So the daughter of Jephthah, her life now vowed to the Lord, went with her companions and bewailed her virginity upon the mountains: not her death, but that she would never know a man.

She returned unto her father, he did with her according to his vow, “and she knew no man.” If she had been put to death there would be no reason for the scripture to say she knew no man. Israel did not do human sacrifices; that was Molech worship among the Canaanites. She was presented to the Lord to serve him, and she remained a virgin.

precepts.text: Jephthah is thrust out as the son of a strange woman, that strange woman being likened to an harlot.
precepts.point: The ways of a man are before the eyes of the Most High and He ponders all his goings. The wicked man's own iniquities take him and he is held with the cords of his sins, dying without instruction in the greatness of his folly.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?” Jephthah shows what comes of it. “Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah.” When Gilead's wife's sons grew up, “they thrust out Jephthah, and said unto him, Thou shalt not inherit in our father’s house; for thou art the son of a strange woman.”

Jephthah is thrust out as the son of a strange woman, and that strange woman is likened to an harlot. The strange woman carries a double meaning, a woman of another nation and a woman outside of your own wife, and Jephthah's mother was that harlot outside the wife.

The son of the strange woman lost his inheritance in his father's house. That is the cord of his father's sin holding the next generation.
